Mindboggle mbhard — landmark detection, matching and physical-space display

Generated 2026-09-14 16:38 by scripts/landmarks_mbhard_report.py. All coordinates are physical LPS millimetres computed through syntx.landmarks.spatial; images are never reoriented — display orientation and keypoint overlays are derived from the direction cosine matrices. Preprocessing: ANTsTorch N4 + non-local-means denoising on MPS, then foreground 2–98% normalisation. Detection: detect_sift3d, 10 scales from 1 to 8 mm, relative threshold 0.002, NMS radius 3 mm, at most 2000 keypoints per image; foreground-masked; 512-D physical-space descriptors. Matching: Lowe ratio 0.95 + mutual nearest neighbour → RANSAC affine, inlier threshold 8.0 mm. Inter-subject pairs are related non-rigidly, so the affine is a consensus filter; agreement of DKT31+aseg whole-brain labels at matched endpoints (chance level shown) is the accuracy proxy.

Example 1 — native pair

Fixed and moving are stored in different native frames (LAS vs RPS arrays, 1.0 vs 1.2 mm x-spacing).

Descriptor / matching: axis-aligned in a globally estimated frame (PCA-seeded iterative search, winner 'identity', rotation 0.0°).

Global rotation search

Hypotheses fixed→moving: identity plus the four principal-axis alignments of the two landmark clouds. Each is refined iteratively (descriptors rebuilt in the current frame → match → rigid RANSAC → rotation), coarse-to-fine over the strongest 25% → 50% → 100% of keypoints; the converged hypothesis with most rigid inliers wins.

Example 2 — fixed rotated +30°, moving rotated −30° about the superior axis

Both volumes (and their label maps) were resampled onto their own grids after a rigid rotation about the z axis through each centre of mass, so the two heads now differ by ≈60° of yaw in physical space. The axis-aligned SIFT3D descriptor tolerates roughly 30° of relative rotation, so plain matching fails here; match_sift3d_with_rotation_search seeds a global fixed→moving rotation from the principal axes of the two landmark clouds and refines it iteratively (descriptors rebuilt in the current frame → match → rigid RANSAC → rotation; coarse-to-fine over keypoint strength). The figures use that pipeline; the plain variants are tabulated for comparison. The recovered affine is also compared with the one predicted from Example 1 and the known rotations (M₂ ≈ Tm⁻¹ · M₁ · Tf).

Descriptor / matching: axis-aligned in a globally estimated frame (PCA-seeded iterative search, winner 'pca3', rotation 61.4°).
